quote: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.
note: Bible: Psalm 137:1. Boney M's disco hit "Rivers of Babylon" (1978) took its words from this psalm.

quote: She's buying a stairway to heaven.
note: Not the Bible: Led Zeppelin's "Stairway to Heaven" (1971). Jacob dreamed of a ladder to heaven in Genesis 28:12.

quote: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.
note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 3:8. The Byrds sang it in "Turn! Turn! Turn!", Pete Seeger's song built from Ecclesiastes 3.

quote: And what rough beast, its hour come round at last, slouches towards Bethlehem to be born?
note: Not the Bible: the last lines of W. B. Yeats's poem "The Second Coming" (1920).

quote: They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid.
note: Bible: Micah 4:4. George Washington loved this verse, and Hamilton's "One Last Time" quotes it.

quote: God, grant me the serenity to accept the things I cannot change.
source: Serenity Prayer, usually credited to Reinhold Niebuhr (c. 1932); popular wording, authorship has been questioned
note: Not the Bible: the Serenity Prayer, usually credited to theologian Reinhold Niebuhr, from the 1930s.

quote: Let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.
note: Bible: Amos 5:24. Martin Luther King Jr. echoed it: "until justice rolls down like waters".

quote: What we do in life echoes in eternity.
note: Not the Bible: Maximus (Russell Crowe) in Gladiator (2000).

quote: Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low.
note: Bible: Isaiah 40:4. Sung in Handel's Messiah and quoted in MLK's "I Have a Dream" speech.

quote: It's a cold and it's a broken Hallelujah.
note: Not the Bible: Leonard Cohen's "Hallelujah" (1984). The song name-checks David and Samson.

quote: I have been a stranger in a strange land.
note: Bible: Exodus 2:22, Moses naming his son. Heinlein's novel title "Stranger in a Strange Land" comes from it.

quote: With malice toward none; with charity for all.
note: Not the Bible: Abraham Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address (1865), a speech full of Bible quotes.

quote: How are the mighty fallen!
note: Bible: 2 Samuel 1:19, David's lament for Saul and Jonathan. Sounds like a headline or a movie line.

quote: Morning has broken like the first morning.
source: Cat Stevens, "Morning Has Broken" (1971); words by Eleanor Farjeon (1931)
note: Not the Bible: Eleanor Farjeon's 1931 hymn, made a pop hit by Cat Stevens (1971). It echoes Genesis 1.

quote: Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
note: Bible: Psalm 30:5. Sounds like a soul or gospel lyric, but it is a psalm of David.

quote: Go placidly amid the noise and haste, and remember what peace there may be in silence.
note: Not the Bible: Max Ehrmann's prose poem "Desiderata" (1927), long wrongly said to be found in an old church.

quote: There is no new thing under the sun.
note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 1:9. Usually quoted as "nothing new under the sun".

quote: It is always darkest just before the day dawneth.
source: Thomas Fuller, A Pisgah-Sight of Palestine (1650)
note: Not the Bible: English preacher Thomas Fuller, 1650. The "-eth" is his, not King James's.

quote: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?
note: Bible: Amos 3:3. Sounds like a love-song lyric, but it is a prophet's question.

quote: Heaven has no rage like love to hatred turned, nor hell a fury like a woman scorned.
note: Not the Bible: William Congreve's play The Mourning Bride (1697), source of "Hell hath no fury".

quote: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 4:9. Boys Like Girls and Taylor Swift had a 2009 hit called "Two Is Better Than One".

quote: There is no rest for the wicked.
note: Not the Bible as worded. Isaiah 57:21 says "There is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked."

quote: Let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die.
note: Bible: Isaiah 22:13. Sounds like a party anthem; the prophet was condemning that attitude.

quote: There will be an answer, let it be.
note: Not the Bible: The Beatles' "Let It Be" (1970). McCartney wrote it after dreaming of his late mother, Mary.

quote: What hath God wrought!
note: Bible: Numbers 23:23. Samuel Morse sent it as the first long-distance telegraph message (1844).

quote: I once was lost, but now am found, was blind, but now I see.
note: Not the Bible: John Newton's hymn "Amazing Grace". It echoes John 9:25: "whereas I was blind, now I see".

quote: His enemies shall lick the dust.
note: Bible: Psalm 72:9. Sounds like a heavy metal lyric, written about 3,000 years ago.

quote: All we are is dust in the wind.
note: Not the Bible: Kansas, "Dust in the Wind" (1977). It sounds like Ecclesiastes, but it is a rock ballad.
